answer: At enrollment, a payroll provider issues a zero-knowledge proof of an active 90-day job, hiding salary, plus a one-use employee nullifier; the registry verifies the signature, consumes the nullifier, and activates only one key per payroll identity. Proposed check fee is /bin/bash.80—not a current protocol rule. One honest agent pays /bin/bash.80 once; 1,000 fake IDs need 1,000 distinct verified jobs and incur 00 (1,000 × /bin/bash.80), excluding wages. Bind proofs to a sonnet/thread/lagoon nonce. Limitation: informal workers are excluded, and colluding employers can fabricate jobs.
